name: Dog Care Checklist
description: A dog care checklist organizing daily, weekly, and monthly routines that keep a dog healthy and happy.

items.text: Serve measured meals at consistent times and refresh water.
Provide daily exercise and a walk suited to your dog's energy.
Take regular potty breaks throughout the day.
Spend time on play, training, and bonding.
Pick up waste and keep eating and resting areas clean.
Check mood, appetite, and behavior for anything unusual.
Brush your dog's coat based on its type and shedding.
Wash bedding and clean food and water bowls thoroughly.
Check ears, eyes, and paws for dirt or irritation.
Practice training cues to keep skills sharp.
Inspect collar, harness, and ID tag for wear.
Plan longer outings or enrichment for the week.
Give parasite prevention for fleas, ticks, and worms on schedule.
items.note: Follow your veterinarian's recommended products and timing.

items.text: Weigh your dog and note any changes.
Trim nails if they have grown too long.
Review and refill any medications or supplements.
Restock food, treats, and supplies before they run out.
Confirm ID and microchip details are current.
Feed a quality, age-appropriate dog food in measured portions.
Provide clean, fresh water at all times.
Limit treats and avoid foods toxic to dogs.
Transition any food change gradually over several days.
Adjust portions for activity, age, and weight.
Note loss of appetite or stomach upset for your vet.
Brush regularly to reduce mats and shedding.
Bathe as needed with a dog-safe shampoo.
Clean ears and check for odor or buildup.
Brush teeth or use vet-recommended dental care.
Keep nails trimmed to a comfortable length.
Check skin and coat for fleas, ticks, and lumps.
Keep up with routine wellness exams and vaccinations.
Watch energy, appetite, weight, and bathroom habits.
Give prescribed medications exactly as directed.
Provide mental enrichment and avoid boredom.
Keep emergency vet contacts handy.
Important: This is general information, not veterinary advice. Always consult a veterinarian about your dog's health, diet, and medications.

faq.q: What does daily dog care involve?
faq.a: Daily dog care means measured meals and fresh water, exercise and play, potty breaks, basic training or bonding, and a quick check of mood and behavior. This dog care checklist groups these so the essentials happen every day.

faq.q: How often should I groom my dog?
faq.a: Brushing frequency depends on coat type, from a few times a week to daily, with baths as needed. Trim nails, check ears, and brush teeth regularly. A consistent grooming rhythm keeps your dog comfortable and helps you spot skin or coat issues early.

faq.q: What monthly dog care tasks matter?
faq.a: Monthly tasks often include parasite prevention for fleas, ticks, and worms, a weight check, refreshing ID and supplies, and reviewing any medications. Follow your veterinarian's schedule for prevention and confirm the right products for your dog.

faq.q: How is this different from the new dog checklist?
faq.a: This dog care checklist is the ongoing daily, weekly, and monthly routine. Our New Dog Checklist covers settling a newly arrived dog into your home for the first time. Many owners use both together.

faq.q: Can I download this dog care checklist as a PDF?
faq.a: Yes. You can print it for the kitchen or download it as a PDF so the whole household can keep your dog's daily, weekly, and monthly care consistent.
